questions.question: Under the null hypothesis ($H_0$) of the Hausman specification test comparing Fixed Effects (FE) and Random Effects (RE) panel data estimators, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Both FE and RE estimators are consistent, but the RE estimator is asymptotically efficient.
Only the FE estimator is consistent, while the RE estimator is inconsistent.
Both FE and RE estimators are inconsistent due to unobserved heterogeneity.
The RE estimator is consistent and efficient, but the FE estimator is inconsistent.

questions.question: In a binary probit model $P(Y=1|X) = \Phi(X\beta)$, where $\Phi(\cdot)$ is the standard normal cumulative distribution function, how is the marginal effect of a continuous regressor $X_j$ calculated?
options: It is constant and equal to the coefficient $\beta_j$.
It is given by $\phi(X\beta)\beta_j$, where $\phi(\cdot)$ is the standard normal probability density function.
It is equal to $\ln(\beta_j) \Phi(X\beta)$ and is restricted to be positive.
It is calculated as $\Phi(\beta_j)$ and does not depend on the values of the other regressors.

questions.question: Unlike Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) which minimizes the sum of squared residuals, linear Quantile Regression for the $\tau$-th conditional quantile (where $\tau \in (0,1)$) estimates parameters by minimizing which objective function?
options: \sum_{i=1}^n (y_i - x_i'\beta)^2 \cdot \tau
\sum_{i=1}^n |y_i - x_i'\beta|^\tau
\sum_{i=1}^n \rho_\tau(y_i - x_i'\beta), \text{ where } \rho_\tau(u) = u(\tau - \mathbb{I}(u < 0)) \text{ is the check loss function}
\sum_{i=1}^n \ln(1 + e^{\tau(y_i - x_i'\beta)})

questions.question: Consider a standard Type I Tobit model $y_i^* = x_i'\beta + \varepsilon_i$ with $y_i = \max(0, y_i^*)$. If an economist estimates this model using Ordinary Least Squares (OLS) on the full sample (including zero values), what is the statistical consequence on the resulting parameter estimates?
options: The estimates remain unbiased and consistent, but standard errors are underestimated.
The estimates remain unbiased, but suffer from extreme variance inflation.
The estimates are consistent only if the proportion of zero observations exceeds 50%.
The estimates are biased and attenuated toward zero due to sample censoring.

questions.question: In Vector Autoregression (VAR) analysis, applying a recursive identification scheme via Cholesky decomposition of the error covariance matrix implies which of the following?
options: The contemporaneous matrix of structural interactions is lower triangular, making the ordering of variables in the VAR system consequential for impulse response functions.
All variables in the system affect each other contemporaneously with equal magnitude.
Long-run restrictions are automatically imposed such that all shocks have strictly transitory effects.
The reduced-form errors across all equations are assumed to be uncorrelated without requiring structural assumptions.
